主要内容: On May 6, 2015, the U.S. Department of the Treasury announced it would offer $64 billion in Treasury securities to refund approximately $67 billion in maturing Treasury notes due on May 15, 2015. This action is expected to result in a debt pay down of about $3 billion. The refunding includes a $24 billion 3-year note maturing on May 15, 2018; a $24 billion 10-year note maturing on May 15, 2025; and a $16 billion 30-year bond maturing on May 15, 2045. These securities will be auctioned on May 12, 13, and 14, 2015, with settlements on May 15, 2015. The Treasury also outlined plans to meet remaining financing needs through various auctions and operations, including a test buyback operation conducted on April 16, 2015. The Treasury plans to maintain current coupon issuance levels and adjust as needed based on projected financing needs. Additionally, the Treasury will increase the supply of Treasury bills to enhance market functioning and liquidity, while maintaining its strategy to extend the weighted average maturity of the debt. The Treasury also stated its intention to hold a cash balance sufficient to cover one week of outflows, subject to a minimum balance of $150 billion, as part of its updated cash management policy. The U.S. Department of the Treasury issued a statement on May 6, 2015, regarding the debt limit and the government's ability to meet its obligations. The debt limit does not authorize new spending but allows the government to finance existing legal obligations. The Temporary Debt Limit Extension Act suspended the debt limit through March 15, 2015. Since March 16, the U.S. has reached its statutory debt limit. The Treasury suspended the sale of State and Local Government Series securities to avoid exceeding the limit. Congress did not act to raise the debt limit, so the Treasury implemented extraordinary measures to continue financing the government. These measures provide temporary headroom under the debt limit. The Treasury emphasized that Congress is responsible for extending the nation’s borrowing authority and urged Congress to raise the debt limit as soon as possible. The next quarterly refunding announcement was scheduled for August 5, 2015.
